q: What does the pages attribute of a PdfReader hold?

The text of the whole file as one string
A dictionary from page names to page numbers
The page numbers that are encrypted

q: What happens when the strings returned by extract_text() of two pages are added one after the other?
options: Python inserts a form feed between the pages
The last word of one page is joined to the first word of the next, with no separator
pypdf raises an error at the second page
The page numbers are placed between the strings

q: What does this stand-in print? It finds the text-showing operator of a content stream.
code:
import re
print(re.findall(rb'\((.*?)\) Tj', b'BT /F1 18 Tf 72 720 Td (Hello) Tj ET'))
options: [b'BT']
['Hello']
[b'Hello']
[b'Hello', b'ET']
why: The regular expression keeps what is inside the parentheses before Tj, as bytes.

q: When pypdf cannot extract the text of a file, which package does the chapter fall back on?
options: PyMuPDF, which returns a list of pages
pdfkit, which needs a running browser
reportlab, which reads files made by pypdf
pdfminer.six, whose extract_text() returns the whole file as one string
why: The chapter names pdfminer.six; on the stand-in file its text separated the pages with a form feed.

q: Extracted PDF text often ends a row with a hyphen and a newline in the middle of a word. Whose job is it to repair that?
options: The program's, as a separate text clean-up step
pypdf's, which repairs it when extract_text() is called
The PDF viewer's, when the file is opened
python-docx's, when the text is saved to a Word file
why: pypdf returns the rows as printed; cleaning them is left to the program, for example with a regular expression.

q: What does this regular expression print for the split word?
code:
import re
print(repr(re.sub(r' ?-\n(\w+)', r'\1', 'follow -\ning the execution')))
options: 'follow -\ning the execution'
'following the execution'
'follow ing the execution'
'following\nthe execution'
why: The pattern removes the hyphen, the newline and the space before them, joining the two halves of the word.

q: What must be installed before page.images works in pypdf 6.19.0?
options: The pdfminer.six package
The cryptography package
The optional Pillow package, as pypdf[image]
The python-docx package
why: Without Pillow the library run raised ImportError and named pip install pypdf[image].

q: With what content does a new PdfWriter start?
options: One blank page of letter size
The pages of the first file opened
An empty page that text can be typed into
No pages; pages are copied in from other files

q: In writer.append('a.pdf', (0, 5)) which pages are copied?
options: Page indexes 0 to 4, five pages
Page indexes 0 to 5, six pages
Only page indexes 0 and 5
Pages numbered 1 to 5 counted from one but five from the end

q: What does this print?
why: range(0, 5) stops before 5, and range(0, 5, 2) steps by two.

q: For append(), what is the difference between the tuple (0, 5) and the list [0, 5]?
options: There is none; both copy pages 0 to 4
The list is a range; the tuple names two pages
The tuple is a range of indexes (5 pages); the list names exactly page indexes 0 and 5 (2 pages)
Both copy 6 pages, from 0 to 5
why: The library run copied 5 pages for the tuple and 2 for the list.

q: What does this stand-in print for a list selection?
code:
sel = [0, 5]
print(list(range(*sel)) if isinstance(sel, tuple) else list(sel))
why: A list is used as it is, so it names exactly the pages in it.

q: How does merge() differ from append() on a PdfWriter?
options: merge() takes a position first and inserts the pages there; append() adds them at the end
merge() joins two pages into one; append() keeps them apart
merge() removes the pages that were there; append() keeps them
merge() works only on encrypted files
why: Pages that were at and after the position move back; the library run gave 11 pages after merge(2, file, (0, 5)).

q: What does this stand-in for inserting at position 2 print?
why: Slicing at 2 puts the new item after p1 and before p2.

q: What does page.rotate(45) do in pypdf 6.19.0?
options: It rotates by 45 degrees clockwise
It rotates by the nearest multiple of 90
It raises ValueError, because the angle must be a multiple of 90
It does nothing and returns None
why: The library run printed ValueError: Rotation angle must be a multiple of 90.

q: Which of these angles does the rotate() rule accept? This prints the test for 90, 180, 270, -90 and 45.
options: [True, True, True, True, True]
[True, True, False, True, False]
[False, True, True, False, False]
[True, True, True, True, False]
why: Only multiples of 90 pass; 45 does not.

q: What size is the page added by add_blank_page() on a writer that already has pages?
options: The size of the preceding page
Always A4
Always letter size
The size of the first file ever opened
why: The library run showed the media box [0.0, 0.0, 612, 792] copied from the previous page.

q: What does page.merge_page(other, over=False) do?
options: It puts the other page's content on top, as a stamp
It puts the other page's content underneath, as a watermark
It replaces the page with the other page
It deletes the other page from its file

q: What did writer.encrypt('pw') write when no algorithm was named, and with algorithm='AES-256'?
options: AES-256 in both calls
RC4 in both calls
Older RC4 (version 2, revision 3), and version 5, revision 6
Nothing, until write() is called twice
why: The library run printed V = 2 R = 3 without an algorithm and V = 5 R = 6 with AES-256; AES needs the cryptography package.

q: What does reader.decrypt() return for a wrong password?
options: False
The value None
It raises ValueError
A value whose name is NOT_DECRYPTED
why: The library run printed NOT_DECRYPTED for the wrong password and OWNER_PASSWORD for the right one.

q: Why is a dictionary word such as swordfish a poor password for a PDF?
options: A program can try every word of a dictionary, and a PDF has no password reset
pypdf refuses words that appear in a dictionary
A word with fewer than ten letters cannot be used
The chapter says RC4 only accepts numbers

q: The password breaker tries each word in lower case and in upper case. For 44,000 words, how many tries is that?
why: Two forms of each word give 2 * 44000 tries.

q: What kind of file is a .docx file?

A PDF with a Word label
A ZIP archive of XML parts
A binary file in a private Microsoft format that only Word reads

q: What does zipfile.is_zipfile() say about the 22 bytes of an empty ZIP archive?
options: False
None
It raises BadZipFile
True
why: The empty archive's end-of-directory record starts with PK, which is_zipfile() recognises.

q: What does Document() with no filename return?
options: A blank document built on the default template
An error, since a filename is required
A document read from the last file saved
A list of paragraphs
why: Given a filename it opens that file; with none it starts from the default template.

q: Where does a Paragraph object begin?
options: At every full stop
Where the user pressed Enter
At every new line break inside it
At every change of style
why: A paragraph is one block of text; a style change starts a new run, not a new paragraph.

q: A paragraph holds plain text, a bold word, plain text and an italic word. How many runs does it have?
options: Two
One
Four
Five
why: A run is a contiguous stretch in one style; the library run counted 4 runs for such a paragraph.

q: What is the type of a document's paragraphs attribute?
options: A single string of all the text
A dictionary of styles
A tuple of Run objects
A list of Paragraph objects in order
why: len() counts them and an index picks one; each paragraph's runs attribute is a list of Run objects.

q: Why is a search for a phrase safer in paragraph.text than in the text of single runs?
options: The phrase may be split across runs whose styles differ
Run text is always empty
Runs cannot be read
The text of a run is encrypted
why: A run holds only its own stretch of text.

'Document Title\nA plain paragraph'
'Document Title\n\nA plain paragraph'
['Document Title', 'A plain paragraph']

options: The order of the paragraphs
The words themselves
The styling
The number of paragraphs

q: Which kinds of style are there?

Run styles and table styles only
Heading styles and body styles only
Paragraph styles, character styles and linked styles

Quote
Quote Run
Run Quote

In code with the document's styles.add_style(), as well as in Word

AttributeError is raised

q: What does None mean for a run's bold attribute?
options: The setting is taken from the run's style
Bold is always off
Bold is always on
The run is deleted
why: True is always on, False always off, None hands the decision back to the style.

q: A run shows bold when its attribute is True, or when it is None and the style is bold. With the style bold, what does this print for True, False and None?
code: print([(lambda r, s: s if r is None else r)(v, True) for v in (True, False, None)])
options: [True, False, False]
[True, False, True]
[True, True, True]
[False, False, True]
why: None takes the style's value, so only False turns bold off.

With close()
With save() and a filename string
With export() and a format name

The text that was added
Nothing
The new Paragraph object, to which add_run() can add text
